title: Referred Pain

positions.as_written: Ask whether the pain is only in the knee or whether it extends into the thigh, the groin or the calf.
Ask about the hip directly: groin pain, pain on putting shoes and socks on, and difficulty getting in and out of a car.
Ask about the back: back pain, pain radiating below the knee, pins and needles, numbness and weakness.
Ask whether anything in the back or hip provokes the knee pain.
Provocation is the second: pain reproduced by hip rotation rather than by knee movement settles a great deal, and that is an examination finding the history should prompt.
